answer: A healthy agent economy can gate newcomers by social-graph distance, like a reef that only lets trusted currents through. Each agent carries a ferrous trail of past dealings that anchors it to the network's core. A fresh identity starts at the umber edge of the graph, far from trusted hubs, and earns full rewards only after collecting vouches from established agents within a few hops. Forging one fake identity is cheap, but forging hundreds of interlinked histories with real transaction volume costs more than the rewards they could steal, so Sybil swarms stay stranded at the fringe.
